requirements.title: Minimal workspace record
requirements.rationale: The rule needs a workspace's owner, organization, kind, parent and status before the routes that create workspaces exist.

criteria.condition: a workspace record with slug, owner_id, org_id, kind, parent_slug and status is inserted
criteria.action: persist the record so that every later read by that slug returns the same six values, also after the store is closed and opened again
criteria.contract: the read returns found = true and a record equal to the inserted one, with no error

setup: a store opened on an empty directory from t.TempDir(), migrated to the current schema
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/record_test.go, a table over {repository record with parent_slug null in each of the five statuses; fork record whose parent is the repository}: insert(rec); got, found, err = get(rec.slug); assert err == nil and found and got == rec; close the store, open it again on the same directory; assert get(rec.slug) == rec

criteria.condition: a record is inserted whose slug already has a record
criteria.action: refuse the insert and leave the stored record unchanged
criteria.contract: the insert returns the duplicate-slug error; a read by that slug returns the first record

setup: a migrated store holding the repository record 'acme' owned by user u1
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/record_test.go: err = insert({slug:'acme', owner_id:u2, ...}); assert errors.Is(err, the duplicate-slug error); assert get('acme').owner_id == u1

criteria.condition: a record is inserted that has an empty slug, owner_id or org_id, a kind other than repository or fork, a status other than pending, cloning, ready, failed or archived, kind repository with a parent_slug, kind fork without a parent_slug, kind fork whose parent has no record or is itself a fork, or kind fork whose org_id differs from its parent's org_id
criteria.action: refuse the insert and write nothing
criteria.contract: the insert returns the invalid-record error; a read by the refused slug returns found = false

setup: a migrated store holding the repository record 'acme' in org o1 and its fork 'acme--f1'
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/record_test.go, a table with one row per case named in the condition (empty slug; empty owner_id; empty org_id; kind 'mirror'; status 'deleted'; repository with parent_slug 'acme'; fork with parent_slug null; fork with parent_slug 'nope'; fork with parent_slug 'acme--f1'; fork of 'acme' with org_id o2): err = insert(row); assert errors.Is(err, the invalid-record error); assert the number of stored records is still 2

criteria.condition: a record is read by a string that no record has as its slug, including the empty string, a string of 300 characters and a string that differs from an existing slug only in letter case
criteria.action: report that no such workspace exists as a result and not as a failure
criteria.contract: the read returns found = false and a nil error

setup: a migrated store holding the repository record 'acme'
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/record_test.go, a table over {'', 'nope', 'ACME', 'acme--x', 300 times 'a'}: _, found, err = get(s); assert err == nil and not found

requirements.title: Access level on a repository workspace
requirements.rationale: Every later answer depends on one resolution of who the caller is to the workspace (PLAT-FR-060 step 1, section 3.3.6).

criteria.condition: the caller is the admin token and the slug names a repository workspace
criteria.action: resolve the level admin
criteria.contract: level = admin

setup: a store holding repository workspace 'acme' with owner u-owner in org o1, and 'solo' with owner u-owner in org o2
a membership stub: u-member and u-owner are members of active org o1; u-blocked-org-member is a member of org o3, which is blocked; nobody is a member of o2
workspace 'held' with owner u-owner in blocked org o3, and 'orphan' with owner u-owner in org o9, which does not exist
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/level_test.go, one table of (caller, slug, want level) run through the level resolver: (admin token, 'acme', admin); (admin token, 'held', admin); (u-owner, 'acme', owner); (u-owner, 'solo', owner); (u-owner, 'held', owner); (u-owner, 'orphan', owner); (u-member, 'acme', member); (u-member, 'solo', none); (u-blocked-org-member, 'held', none); (u-ghost, whose membership row names the deleted org o9 and whom the stub therefore reports as a member of no active org, 'orphan', none); (u-stranger, 'acme', none); (u-admin-role with no membership, authenticated by API key, 'acme', none); (u-admin-role authenticated by PAT, 'acme', none); (u-member authenticated by PAT, 'acme', member); then for each status in {pending, cloning, ready, failed, archived} insert a workspace in o1 owned by u-owner and assert admin token -> admin, u-owner -> owner, u-member -> member, u-stranger -> none

criteria.condition: the caller is a user whose id equals the workspace's owner_id
criteria.action: resolve the level owner, whether or not the user is also a member of the workspace's organization and whether that organization is active, blocked or absent
criteria.contract: level = owner

criteria.condition: the caller is a user who is not the workspace's owner and is a member of the workspace's organization, and that organization has status active
criteria.action: resolve the level member
criteria.contract: level = member

criteria.condition: the workspace's organization is blocked or no longer exists
criteria.action: resolve the level none for every user who is not the workspace's owner, including users who hold a membership of that organization
criteria.contract: level = none

criteria.action: for any user with role admin who is neither the workspace's owner nor a member of its active organization, resolve the level none, with an API key as with a PAT
criteria.contract: level = none

criteria.action: for any caller and any workspace, resolve the same level in each of the statuses pending, cloning, ready, failed and archived, and the same level whether a user authenticated with an API key or a PAT

requirements.title: Access level on a task fork
requirements.rationale: A task fork never grants more than its parent, so leaving an organization also closes the forks created in it (PLAT-FR-060 step 1, WS-FR-004).

criteria.condition: the caller is a user whose id equals a fork's owner_id and whose level on the fork's parent is member or owner
criteria.action: resolve the level owner on the fork
criteria.contract: level = owner

setup: a store holding repository 'acme' (owner u-owner, org o1, active) and forks 'acme--m' (owner u-member), 'acme--o' (owner u-owner), 'acme--gone' (owner u-left)
a membership stub: u-member and u-other are members of o1; u-left is a member of nothing
repository 'held' (owner u-owner, blocked org o3) with fork 'held--m' (owner u-blocked-org-member, a member of o3)
a fork row 'lost--f' (owner u-member, org o1) whose parent row 'lost' was removed directly in the store after the insert
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/level_test.go, one table of (caller, fork slug, want level) run through the level resolver: (u-member, 'acme--m', owner); (u-owner, 'acme--o', owner); (u-owner, 'acme--m', owner); (u-other, 'acme--m', member); (u-member, 'acme--o', member); (u-left, 'acme--gone', none); (u-blocked-org-member, 'held--m', none); (u-owner, 'held--m', owner); (u-stranger, 'acme--m', none); (admin token, 'acme--m', admin); (admin token, 'acme--gone', admin); (u-member, 'lost--f', none); (admin token, 'lost--f', admin); and for every row with a user caller assert that want == none whenever the resolver gives none for that user on the fork's parent

criteria.condition: the caller is the user who owns a fork's parent and the fork is owned by another user
criteria.action: resolve the level owner on the fork
criteria.contract: level = owner

criteria.condition: the caller is a user whose level on a fork's parent is member and who owns neither the fork nor its parent
criteria.action: resolve the level member on the fork
criteria.contract: level = member

criteria.action: for any user whose level on a fork's parent is none, resolve the level none on the fork, including for the user who owns the fork
criteria.contract: level = none

criteria.condition: the caller is the admin token and the slug names a fork
criteria.action: resolve the level admin
criteria.contract: level = admin

criteria.condition: the slug names a fork whose parent has no record and the caller is a user
criteria.action: resolve the level none
criteria.contract: level = none, with no error

requirements.title: Decision for a declared need
requirements.rationale: Each workspace route states what it needs once, and the caller sees one of three answers (PLAT-FR-060 steps 2 to 4).

criteria.condition: a request reaches a workspace route that declares need read, write or owner and the caller's level on the named workspace is admin or owner
criteria.action: grant access, run the route's handler and make the decision readable by it
criteria.contract: the handler runs once; the decision it reads holds the level as the string admin or owner and the workspace record of the slug in the path

setup: a store holding repository 'acme' (owner u-owner, org o1) in status ready and 'old' (owner u-owner, org o1) in status archived
a membership stub: u-member is a member of active org o1

an httptest server with three probe routes GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/r, /w and /o registered through package 02's route registration with this package's need mark set to read, write and owner, behind the access check installed in the pipeline's access position; the probe handler writes 200 with the decision's level and record slug; a test hook sets the authenticated caller
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/middleware_test.go, a table of (caller, slug, route, want status, want error_type, want message, want level): for admin token and u-owner on 'acme' and 'old', every route -> 200 and body level == 'admin' / 'owner' and body slug == the path slug; u-member on /r of 'acme' and 'old' -> 200, level 'member'; u-member on /w and /o of 'acme' and of archived 'old' -> 403, 'forbidden', 'org members have read-only access to this workspace'; u-stranger on every route of 'acme', and each of admin token, u-owner, u-member and u-stranger on every route of 'nope' -> 404, 'not_found', 'workspace not found'; for every refused row assert the probe handler's call counter did not move and the body is the error envelope with code == status and Content-Type 'application/json; charset=utf-8'

criteria.condition: a request reaches a workspace route that declares need read and the caller's level is member
criteria.action: grant access, run the route's handler and make the decision readable by it
criteria.contract: the handler runs once; the decision it reads holds the level as the string member and the workspace record

criteria.condition: a request reaches a workspace route that declares need write or owner and the caller's level is member, in any status of the workspace including archived
criteria.action: refuse the request without running the route's handler
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden and message 'org members have read-only access to this workspace'; the handler is not called

criteria.condition: a request reaches a workspace route with any need and the caller's level is none or the slug names no workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request without running the route's handler
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found and message 'workspace not found'; the handler is not called

criteria.condition: reading the workspace record, the parent's record or the caller's memberships fails while a decision is being made
criteria.action: refuse the request without running the route's handler and without granting access
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with error_type internal; the handler is not called; the response body contains neither the workspace record nor the text of the underlying failure

setup: the probe routes of the decision table test
a record reader and a membership stub that can each be told to return an error containing the text 'disk I/O error at /data/parley.db'
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/middleware_test.go, a table over {record read fails for the slug; record read fails for the fork's parent; membership read fails} x {admin token where the failing read is on its path, u-owner, u-member, u-stranger} x {read, write, owner}: r = get(route); assert r.status == 500 and r.json.error.error_type == 'internal' and r.json.error.code == 500; assert handler calls == 0; assert body does not contain '/data/parley.db' or 'acme'

criteria.condition: a request reaches the access step with no authenticated caller attached, or the route declared a need other than read, write or owner
criteria.action: refuse the request without running the route's handler and without granting access
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with error_type internal; the handler is not called

setup: a store holding repository 'acme' owned by u-owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/middleware_test.go: (a) call the read probe route for 'acme' with no caller set on the request; (b) register a probe route whose need mark holds a value outside the three and call it as u-owner; in both assert status == 500, error_type == 'internal', handler calls == 0

requirements.title: Anti-enumeration
requirements.rationale: A caller who may not read a workspace must not learn that it exists (PLAT-FR-061).

criteria.action: for any caller whose level on an existing workspace is none, answer with the same HTTP status and the same response body, byte for byte, as for a slug that names no workspace, for each need read, write and owner, each workspace status and each kind
criteria.contract: HTTP 404; the body bytes equal the body bytes of the answer for a slug with no record

setup: a store holding repository workspaces in org o1 owned by u-owner, one per status (pending, cloning, ready, failed, archived), and a fork of the ready one owned by u-left
a membership stub in which u-stranger and u-left are members of nothing and u-admin-role has role admin and no membership
the probe routes with need read, write and owner
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/middleware_test.go: baseline = for each need, the (status, body bytes) of u-stranger on slug 'does-not-exist'; then a table over callers {u-stranger, u-left, u-admin-role} x every stored slug x need {read, write, owner} x method {GET on the probe}: r = call; assert r.status == 404 and bytes.Equal(r.body, baseline[need].body); assert the three baseline bodies are equal to each other; also for the strings {'ACME', 'a--b--c', 300 times 'a', '%2e%2e'} as slug assert the same status and body

criteria.condition: a caller whose level is none calls a route that declares need write or owner on an existing workspace
criteria.action: answer as for a slug that names no workspace and never with the member's read-only refusal
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found; never HTTP 403

criteria.condition: a caller other than an HTTP route, such as the git server, asks for the decision on a slug and a need and the outcome is not-found
criteria.action: return an outcome that carries no workspace record and no level, and that is equal for an existing workspace the caller cannot read and for a slug with no record
criteria.contract: the returned decision has outcome not_found, a zero record and level none; the two decisions compare equal

setup: a store holding repository 'acme' owned by u-owner in org o1; u-stranger is a member of nothing
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/decide_test.go: a = decide(u-stranger, 'acme', need) and b = decide(u-stranger, 'nope', need) for each need; assert a.outcome == not_found and a == b and a.record is the zero record and a.level == none; assert decide(u-member, 'acme', write).outcome == read_only and decide(u-owner, 'acme', owner).outcome == granted

requirements.title: Member contributions
requirements.rationale: Members may fork, contribute changes, record verdicts and make claims although those routes change state (PLAT-FR-062); the rule must let them through and give the routes the facts their own conditions read.

criteria.condition: a caller whose level is member calls a route that declares need read with the method POST, PATCH, PUT or DELETE
criteria.action: grant access exactly as for GET
criteria.contract: the handler runs once and reads level member

setup: a store holding repository 'acme' (owner u-owner, org o1) and its fork 'acme--m' (owner u-member); u-member is a member of active org o1
probe routes registered for POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE on /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/contrib with need read; the probe handler echoes the decision
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/middleware_test.go, a table over the four methods and the slugs {'acme', 'acme--m'}: r = call as u-member; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.level == 'member' on 'acme' and 'owner' on 'acme--m'; assert r.json.record == {slug, owner_id, org_id, kind, parent_slug, status} of the stored record

criteria.condition: access is granted on a workspace route
criteria.action: give the handler the caller's level and the workspace record's slug, owner_id, org_id, kind, parent_slug and status as read during the decision
criteria.contract: the decision read from the request holds the level and all six record fields, equal to the stored record

criteria.condition: a component asks whether a named user, who need not be the caller, has write access to a workspace
criteria.action: answer yes exactly when that user's level on the workspace is owner, and no when it is member or none or the slug names no workspace
criteria.contract: returns true or false with a nil error; returns an error and false when a read fails

setup: a store holding repository 'acme' (owner u-owner, org o1) and fork 'acme--m' (owner u-member); u-member is a member of active org o1
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/level_test.go, a table of (user, slug, want): (u-owner, 'acme', true); (u-member, 'acme', false); (u-stranger, 'acme', false); (u-member, 'acme--m', true); (u-owner, 'acme--m', true); (u-owner, 'nope', false); then make the record read fail and assert the result is (false, non-nil error)

requirements.title: Readable set
requirements.rationale: The workspace list, events and audit must all show a caller the same workspaces, and never one that would then answer 404 (PLAT-FR-063).

criteria.condition: the readable set is asked for the admin token
criteria.action: return a set that contains every workspace, with level admin
criteria.contract: the set reports all = true; a membership question on any existing slug answers yes with level admin

setup: a store holding: repositories 'mine' (owner u1, org o-u1), 'team' (owner u2, org o1), 'both' (owner u1, org o1), 'held' (owner u2, blocked org o3), 'other' (owner u2, org o2), 'archived-team' (owner u2, org o1, status archived); forks 'mine--x' (owner u3), 'team--a' (owner u1), 'team--b' (owner u3), 'other--z' (owner u1)
a membership stub: u1 is a member of active o-u1 and o1 and of blocked o3; u3 is a member of o-u1 only; u9 is a member of nothing
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/readable_test.go: s = readable(admin token); assert s.all and s.contains(x) with level admin for every stored slug. s = readable(u1); assert s.entries == {mine: owner, mine--x: owner, both: owner, team: member, team--a: owner, team--b: member, archived-team: member} exactly, each slug once; assert 'held', 'other' and 'other--z' are absent. assert readable(u9) is empty with nil error. Then for every user in {u1, u2, u3, u9} and every stored slug assert s.contains(slug) == (level(user, slug) != none) and, when contained, s.level(slug) == level(user, slug)

criteria.condition: the readable set is asked for a user
criteria.action: return the workspaces the user owns, the forks of those workspaces and the workspaces, forks included, of the organizations the user is a member of while those organizations are active, each once and each with the caller's level, in every workspace status
criteria.contract: a set of (slug, level) entries with level owner or member and no duplicate slug

criteria.condition: a workspace is both owned by the user and in an organization the user is a member of
criteria.action: list it once with level owner
criteria.contract: one entry for the slug, level owner

criteria.action: for any user and any workspace, include the workspace in the user's readable set exactly when the user's resolved level on it is not none, with that level, so that a fork whose owner has level none on its parent and a workspace of a blocked organization that the user does not own are absent

criteria.condition: the readable set is asked for a user who owns no workspace and is a member of no active organization
criteria.action: return an empty set
criteria.contract: an empty set with all = false and a nil error

criteria.condition: reading workspace records or memberships fails while the readable set is built
criteria.action: return the failure and no set
criteria.contract: a non-nil error and an empty set with all = false; no partial entries

setup: the store of the readable-set table test, with a record reader and a membership stub that can each be told to fail
check.pseudocode: in internal/access/readable_test.go, a table over {membership read fails, record read fails}: s, err = readable(u1); assert err != nil and len(s.entries) == 0 and not s.all

execution_paths.title: An owner, a member and an outsider call a write route of the same workspace

steps.action: calls a route that declares need write on workspace 'acme', which the developer owns, with an API key
authenticates the caller, reads the workspace record, resolves level owner and runs the handler, which answers 200 with access owner
calls the same route with an API key
resolves level member from the caller's membership in the workspace's active organization and answers 403 forbidden with 'org members have read-only access to this workspace'
as a second user who is neither the owner nor in the organization, calls the same route, and then the same route on a slug that names no workspace
answers both requests 404 not_found with 'workspace not found', with identical bodies

real_components: the net/http router and error envelope of internal/server
the access middleware and level resolver of internal/access
the users, organizations and memberships of internal/identity
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store in t.TempDir()
three users with API keys: the owner, a member of organization o1 and an outsider; workspace record 'acme' owned by the owner in o1
a probe route POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe registered by the test with need write behind the real authentication middleware
end_state: the owner's call answered 200 and the probe handler ran exactly once
the member's call answered 403 with error_type forbidden
the outsider's calls on 'acme' and on 'nope' answered 404 with error_type not_found and byte-identical bodies
smoke.pseudocode: in internal/access/access_integration_test.go: start the hub; create users, org, membership through internal/identity; insert the record; assert post('/api/v1/workspaces/acme/probe', ownerKey).status == 200; m = post(..., memberKey); assert m.status == 403 and m.json.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; a = post('/api/v1/workspaces/acme/probe', outsiderKey); b = post('/api/v1/workspaces/nope/probe', outsiderKey); assert a.status == 404 and b.status == 404 and bytes.Equal(a.body, b.body); assert probe calls == 1

execution_paths.title: A member who leaves the organization loses the fork they created

steps.action: calls a route that declares need owner on task fork 'acme--m', which the member owns, and receives 200 with access owner
removes the member from the workspace's organization
calls the same route on the fork and a read route on the parent 'acme'
resolves level none on the parent, therefore none on the fork, and answers both requests 404 not_found
builds the former member's readable set without 'acme' and 'acme--m'
calls the owner route on the fork as the parent's owner and receives 200 with access owner

real_components: the net/http router and error envelope of internal/server
the access middleware, level resolver and readable set of internal/access
the organization membership removal of internal/identity
setup: the hub, users and workspace of the first path, plus fork record 'acme--m' owned by the member with parent 'acme'
probe routes GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe-read with need read and GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/probe-owner with need owner
end_state: before the removal the member's owner-route call on 'acme--m' answered 200 with level owner
after the removal the member's calls on 'acme--m' and 'acme' answered 404 with error_type not_found
the former member's readable set is empty
the parent's owner still gets 200 with level owner on 'acme--m', and the owner's readable set holds 'acme' and 'acme--m' with level owner
smoke.pseudocode: in internal/access/access_integration_test.go: assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/acme--m/probe-owner', memberKey).json.level == 'owner'; remove the membership through internal/identity; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/acme--m/probe-owner', memberKey).status == 404 and get('/api/v1/workspaces/acme/probe-read', memberKey).status == 404; assert readable(member).entries is empty; assert get('/api/v1/workspaces/acme--m/probe-owner', ownerKey).json.level == 'owner'; assert readable(owner).entries == {acme: owner, acme--m: owner}
